Occurrences.Kwic: 指山門云：豁開戶牖，當軒者誰？紅霞穿碧落，白日繞須彌。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1412.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Gulin Qingmao. Exact actor: Gulin Qingmao. At the mountain gate Gulin Qingmao points and asks who stands at the open doorway, then gives the red-cloud and sun-around-Sumeru line.

Senses.Explanation: The immense moving sky-scene serves as a direct answer or hall declaration rather than as descriptive scenery alone. Chushi Fanqi answers the charge that his words are too tightly sealed; his interlocutor says the line has already travelled throughout the world, and Chushi dismisses even that praise. Yuanwu Keqin gives the couplet when asked what remains after buddhas, patriarchs, sages, and ordinary people are all set aside. Gulin Qingmao uses it at the mountain gate after asking who stands in the opened doorway.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X80/X80n1565.xml). Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元): records Cuiyan's formal address. Cuiyan says ‘as soon as the knowing ear inclines, Xiang Yu crosses east of the river’; the line is his utterance, not documentary narration.

Senses.Explanation: Xiang Yu is the defeated warlord whom Chan addresses invoke at the instant a listener turns an ear or loses the swift horse Wuzhui. Dawei Xing pairs failure to understand with ‘Xiang Yu loses his thousand-li Wuzhui’; Cuiyan's repeated address says that once a knowing listener inclines an ear, ‘Xiang Yu crosses east of the river,’ then warns that taking it that way mistakes a saddle-bridge for one's father's jaw.
